en: Thereafter, having been requested for the sake of the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*) or the empowerment (*abhiṣeka*) of a monastery or similar structure that has been completed, and seeing a great benefit for sentient beings—whether for his own sake or for another’s due to a desire for the means of attaining accomplishments (*siddhi*) and so forth—he should, after encouraging others [to participate], begin the preliminary service (*pūrva-sevā*), which generates the necessary provisions and destroys obstacles, for the purpose of drawing the mandala.

Then, either because he was requested for the purpose of the ultimate consecration that completes the temple and so forth, or because he sought to accomplish his own or others' spiritual attainments (*siddhi*), or because he perceived the great benefit of sentient beings;

Whether prompted by others or not, one should perform the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*) for the purpose of drawing the mandala, for the accumulation of merit, for the destruction of obstacles, and for the subjugation of Māra.
If one who knows the path of the Omniscient One does not achieve accomplishment without practice,
therefore, sitting down free from duality, one should know the reality of the two-fold authentic lineage.
When weary from meditating on the circle of deities, one should recite their mantra;
one should recite one hundred thousand times for the Lord of the Circle, or one hundred thousand times for one's own tutelary deity,
and ten thousand times for the [other] holders of the wheel— this is called the preliminary service.

If the knowledge of the path of omniscience is not cultivated through service, it will not be accomplished. Therefore, abiding in non-duality, one who knows the reality of the two stages should correctly meditate upon the mandala of the deity and recite its secret mantra. One should recite the mantra of the Lord of the Mandala one hundred thousand times, or else one hundred thousand for one's own deity, and ten thousand for those belonging to the mandala.
This is described as the preliminary service.
Thus, the yogi skilled in the three samādhis should perform the preliminary service and the fire offering ten times the number of [mantra] recitations, in accordance with the specific maṇḍala.
Thus, the yogi who is skilled in the three samādhis should also perform the fire offering consisting of one-tenth of the preliminary service (*pūrva-sevā*) in accordance with the maṇḍala.
This is the rule concerning the purpose and application of the preliminary service.
Thus concludes the ritual for the preliminary service, its definitive requirements, and its purpose.
